ref: Dial. 11.1 (chapter XI of Greek; ANF ch. 11)
greek: Οὔτε ἔσται ποτὲ ἄλλος Θεός, ὦ Τρύφων, οὔτε ἦν ἀπ' αἰῶνος,—ἐγὼ οὕτως πρὸς αὐτόν,—πλὴν τοῦ ποιήσαντος καὶ διατάξαντος τόδε τὸ πᾶν. Οὐδὲ ἄλλον μὲν ἡμῶν, ἄλλον δὲ ὑμῶν ἡγούμεθα Θεόν, ἀλλ' αὐτὸν ἐκεῖνον τὸν ἐξαγαγόντα τοὺς πατέρας
greek_edition: W. Trollope (ed.), S. Justini philosophi et martyris cum Tryphone Judaeo dialogus, Cambridge: J. Hall, 1846 (archive.org scan, Greek text with English notes). Greek read from the pdftotext text layer and checked by eye against a 260-dpi render of each PDF page; printed page = running header. Not Otto's text; Trollope's own base text not checked.
english: Justin: There will be no other God, O Trypho, nor was there from eternity any other existing, but He who made and disposed all this universe.
edition: Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 1, Buffalo: Christian Literature Publishing Co., 1885 (New Advent revision, Kevin Knight); chapter numbers only, no page numbers | Greek: Trollope 1846 (Cambridge: J. Hall)
what_it_says: Justin denies any second God and says the Christians and Jews worship the same God who led the fathers out of Egypt.
limits: Monotheism statement only; it says nothing about the Logos. The English omits the Greek parenthesis 'ἐγὼ οὕτως πρὸς αὐτόν'. Opponents cite the 'another God' language later (Dial. 50, 55), not here.

greek: Εἶπεν ὁ κύριος τῷ κυρίῳ μου, Κάθου ἐκ δεξιῶν μου, ἕως ἂν θῶ τοὺς ἐχθρούς σου ὑποπόδιον τῶν ποδῶν σου.
greek_edition: W. Trollope (ed.), S. Justini philosophi et martyris cum Tryphone Judaeo dialogus, Cambridge: J. Hall, 1846 (archive.org scan, Greek text with English notes). Greek read from the pdftotext text layer and checked by eye against a 260-dpi render of each PDF page; printed page = running header. Not Otto's text; Trollope's own base text not checked.
english: The Lord said to My Lord, Sit at My right hand, until I make Your enemies Your footstool.
edition: Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 1, Buffalo: Christian Literature Publishing Co., 1885 (New Advent revision, Kevin Knight); chapter numbers only, no page numbers | Greek: Trollope 1846 (Cambridge: J. Hall)
what_it_says: Justin quotes the LXX of Ps 110:1, where 'the Lord' speaks to a second 'my Lord', and applies it to Christ.
limits: This is a quotation of Scripture, not Justin's own statement; the 'two Lords' sense depends on Justin's exegesis in Dial. 33, and the same Greek word kyrios is used for God in the LXX. Trypho's teachers refer the psalm to Hezekiah (Dial. 33.1).

greek: οὕτως τὸν αἰώνιον αὐτοῦ ἱερέα, καὶ κύριον ὑπὸ τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος καλούμενον, ὁ Θεὸς τῶν ἐν ἀκροβυστίᾳ γενήσεσθαι ἐδήλου
greek_edition: W. Trollope (ed.), S. Justini philosophi et martyris cum Tryphone Judaeo dialogus, Cambridge: J. Hall, 1846 (archive.org scan, Greek text with English notes). Greek read from the pdftotext text layer and checked by eye against a 260-dpi render of each PDF page; printed page = running header. Not Otto's text; Trollope's own base text not checked.
english: so God has shown that His everlasting Priest, called also by the Holy Spirit Lord, would be Priest of those in uncircumcision.
edition: Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 1, Buffalo: Christian Literature Publishing Co., 1885 (New Advent revision, Kevin Knight); chapter numbers only, no page numbers | Greek: Trollope 1846 (Cambridge: J. Hall)
what_it_says: Justin says the Holy Spirit calls the everlasting priest of Ps 110 'Lord' (kyrion), and that God showed this priest would serve the uncircumcised.
limits: The Greek sentence is Justin's own gloss on Ps 110:4; it reports that the Spirit calls the priest kyrios, but it does not state Christ's divinity in metaphysical terms and does not mention the Father-Son relation.

greek: ὁ γὰρ Χριστὸς βασιλεὺς καὶ ἱερεὺς καὶ Θεὸς καὶ κύριος καὶ ἄγγελος καὶ ἄνθρωπος καὶ ἀρχιστράτηγος καὶ λίθος καὶ παιδίον γεννώμενον, καὶ παθητὸς γενόμενος πρῶτον, εἶτα εἰς οὐρανὸν ἀνερχόμενος, καὶ πάλιν παραγινόμενος μετὰ δόξης, καὶ αἰώνιον τὴν βασιλείαν ἔχων κεκήρυκται, ὡς ἀπὸ πασῶν τῶν γραφῶν ἀποδείκνυμι.
greek_edition: W. Trollope (ed.), S. Justini philosophi et martyris cum Tryphone Judaeo dialogus, Cambridge: J. Hall, 1846 (archive.org scan, Greek text with English notes). Greek read from the pdftotext text layer and checked by eye against a 260-dpi render of each PDF page; printed page = running header. Not Otto's text; Trollope's own base text not checked.
english: For Christ is King, and Priest, and God, and Lord, and angel, and man, and captain, and stone, and a Son born, and first made subject to suffering, then returning to heaven, and again coming with glory, and He is preached as having the everlasting kingdom: so I prove from all the Scriptures.
edition: Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 1, Buffalo: Christian Literature Publishing Co., 1885 (New Advent revision, Kevin Knight); chapter numbers only, no page numbers | Greek: Trollope 1846 (Cambridge: J. Hall)
what_it_says: Justin lists 'God' and 'Lord' among the titles of Christ, alongside 'angel', 'man', 'stone' and 'a Son born', and says all Scripture proves it.
limits: A list of titles in which 'God' sits beside 'angel' and 'man'; it does not by itself say what 'God' means here, and it is not the Nicene formula (no homoousios).

ref: Dial. 36.2 (Christ called God and Lord of hosts; Ps 24)
greek: εἰς ἐπίδειξιν ὅτι καὶ Θεὸς καὶ κύριος τῶν δυνάμεων ὁ Χριστὸς καὶ Ἰακὼβ καλεῖται ἐν παραβολῇ ὑπὸ τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος·
greek_edition: W. Trollope (ed.), S. Justini philosophi et martyris cum Tryphone Judaeo dialogus, Cambridge: J. Hall, 1846 (archive.org scan, Greek text with English notes). Greek read from the pdftotext text layer and checked by eye against a 260-dpi render of each PDF page; printed page = running header. Not Otto's text; Trollope's own base text not checked.
english: which I wish to do in order to prove that Christ is called both God and Lord of hosts, and Jacob, in parable by the Holy Spirit;
edition: Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 1, Buffalo: Christian Literature Publishing Co., 1885 (New Advent revision, Kevin Knight); chapter numbers only, no page numbers | Greek: Trollope 1846 (Cambridge: J. Hall)
what_it_says: Justin states the aim of his proof-texts: to show that Christ is called both God and Lord of hosts, and that the Holy Spirit so names him in parable.
limits: 'Called' is a claim about how Scripture names Christ, not a statement of consubstantiality. Opponents will say 'God' here is the title of the Father's agent. The sentence 'Jacob in parable' is a type, not a title.

greek: καὶ ἀποκρίνεται αὐτοῖς τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον, ἢ ἀπὸ προσώπου τοῦ πατρὸς ἢ ἀπὸ τοῦ ἰδίου, Κύριος τῶν δυνάμεων, αὐτὸς οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ βασιλεὺς τῆς δόξης.
greek_edition: W. Trollope (ed.), S. Justini philosophi et martyris cum Tryphone Judaeo dialogus, Cambridge: J. Hall, 1846 (archive.org scan, Greek text with English notes). Greek read from the pdftotext text layer and checked by eye against a 260-dpi render of each PDF page; printed page = running header. Not Otto's text; Trollope's own base text not checked.
english: And the Holy Spirit, either from the person of His Father, or from His own person, answers them, 'The Lord of hosts, He is this King of glory.'
edition: Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 1, Buffalo: Christian Literature Publishing Co., 1885 (New Advent revision, Kevin Knight); chapter numbers only, no page numbers | Greek: Trollope 1846 (Cambridge: J. Hall)
what_it_says: Justin says the Holy Spirit answers the heavenly rulers in Ps 24 with 'the Lord of hosts' and that the answer is either the Father's or the Spirit's own.
limits: Justin does not decide whether the speaker is the Father or the Spirit, so this passage shows the Spirit speaking and called 'Lord of hosts' but not a fixed Trinitarian doctrine; it is a strong text for the Spirit's personal speech, not a clear statement of Trinity.

greek: Καὶ ἐν ἐνενηκοστῷ ὀγδόῳ ψαλμῷ ὀνειδίζει ὑμᾶς τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον, καὶ τοῦτον, ὃν μὴ θέλετε βασιλέα εἶναι, βασιλέα καὶ κύριον καὶ τοῦ Σαμουὴλ καὶ τοῦ Ἀαρὼν καὶ Μωϋσέως καὶ τῶν ἄλλων πάντων ἁπλῶς ὄντα μηνύει.
greek_edition: W. Trollope (ed.), S. Justini philosophi et martyris cum Tryphone Judaeo dialogus, Cambridge: J. Hall, 1846 (archive.org scan, Greek text with English notes). Greek read from the pdftotext text layer and checked by eye against a 260-dpi render of each PDF page; printed page = running header. Not Otto's text; Trollope's own base text not checked.
english: And in the ninety-eighth Psalm, the Holy Spirit reproaches you, and predicts Him whom you do not wish to be king to be King and Lord, both of Samuel, and of Aaron, and of Moses, and, in short, of all the others.
edition: Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 1, Buffalo: Christian Literature Publishing Co., 1885 (New Advent revision, Kevin Knight); chapter numbers only, no page numbers | Greek: Trollope 1846 (Cambridge: J. Hall)
what_it_says: Justin says the Holy Spirit, in Ps 98, reproaches the Jews and announces Christ as King and Lord over Moses, Aaron and Samuel.
limits: The psalm's 'Lord' is read as Christ by Justin's exegesis; the Greek says the Spirit 'announces' him but does not say the Spirit is distinct from the Father in the psalm's own context.

ref: Dial. 38.1 (Trypho's objection: Christ to be worshipped)
greek: καὶ ἀναβεβηκέναι εἰς τὸν οὐρανόν, καὶ πάλιν παραγίνεσθαι ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς, καὶ προσκυνητὸν εἶναι.
greek_edition: W. Trollope (ed.), S. Justini philosophi et martyris cum Tryphone Judaeo dialogus, Cambridge: J. Hall, 1846 (archive.org scan, Greek text with English notes). Greek read from the pdftotext text layer and checked by eye against a 260-dpi render of each PDF page; printed page = running header. Not Otto's text; Trollope's own base text not checked.
english: then that he became man, was crucified, and ascended up to heaven, and comes again to earth, and ought to be worshipped.
edition: Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 1, Buffalo: Christian Literature Publishing Co., 1885 (New Advent revision, Kevin Knight); chapter numbers only, no page numbers | Greek: Trollope 1846 (Cambridge: J. Hall)
what_it_says: Trypho objects that the Christians claim the crucified man ascended and must be worshipped.
limits: Trypho's words, not Justin's; they state the Jewish objection to worship of a human.

ref: Dial. 38.1 (Justin: the wisdom hidden from you; Spirit convicts teachers)
greek: Οἶδα ὅτι, ὡς ὁ τοῦ Θεοῦ λόγος ἔφη, κέκρυπται ἀφ' ὑμῶν ἡ σοφία ἡ μεγάλη αὕτη τοῦ ποιητοῦ τῶν ὅλων καὶ παντοκράτορος Θεοῦ. ... ἐπεὶ οὐ τὰ διὰ τοῦ Θεοῦ ὑπὸ τοῦ προφητικοῦ πνεύματος ἐλέγχονται νοεῖν δυνάμενοι
greek_edition: W. Trollope (ed.), S. Justini philosophi et martyris cum Tryphone Judaeo dialogus, Cambridge: J. Hall, 1846 (archive.org scan, Greek text with English notes). Greek read from the pdftotext text layer and checked by eye against a 260-dpi render of each PDF page; printed page = running header. Not Otto's text; Trollope's own base text not checked.
english: I know that, as the word of God says, this great wisdom of God, the Maker of all things, and the Almighty, is hid from you. ... since they are convicted by the Holy Spirit of inability to perceive the truths taught by God
edition: Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 1, Buffalo: Christian Literature Publishing Co., 1885 (New Advent revision, Kevin Knight); chapter numbers only, no page numbers | Greek: Trollope 1846 (Cambridge: J. Hall)
what_it_says: Justin says that the great wisdom of God, Maker and Almighty, is hidden from the Jews, and that the prophetic Spirit convicts their teachers of being unable to understand what is from God.
limits: 'Wisdom' (sophia) is not identified with the Logos in this passage; the reference to the 'word of God' is to Scripture. The Spirit is the source of the prophecy, not shown to be a person apart from God.

ref: Dial. 38.2 (Ps 45 LXX applied to Christ: worship)
greek: ὅτι αὐτός ἐστι κύριός σου, καὶ προσκυνήσουσιν αὐτῷ.
greek_edition: W. Trollope (ed.), S. Justini philosophi et martyris cum Tryphone Judaeo dialogus, Cambridge: J. Hall, 1846 (archive.org scan, Greek text with English notes). Greek read from the pdftotext text layer and checked by eye against a 260-dpi render of each PDF page; printed page = running header. Not Otto's text; Trollope's own base text not checked.
english: because He is your Lord, they shall worship Him also.
edition: Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 1, Buffalo: Christian Literature Publishing Co., 1885 (New Advent revision, Kevin Knight); chapter numbers only, no page numbers | Greek: Trollope 1846 (Cambridge: J. Hall)
what_it_says: Justin quotes Ps 45 (LXX 44) applied to Christ: the king is 'your Lord' and is to be worshipped.
limits: The verse is Scripture; the Greek of the psalm's 'O God, your throne' is also in this passage but was not separately checked here. Opponents read the 'worship' as honour owed to a king, not divine worship.

ref: Dial. 43.1 (Christ the Son of God born of the Virgin)
greek: παρθένου γεννηθέντα υἱὸν τοῦ Θεοῦ Χριστόν, ὅστις καὶ αἰώνιος νόμος καὶ καινὴ διαθήκη τῷ παντὶ κόσμῳ ἐκηρύσσετο προελευσόμενος, ὡς αἱ προλελεγμέναι προφητεῖαι σημαίνουσι.
greek_edition: W. Trollope (ed.), S. Justini philosophi et martyris cum Tryphone Judaeo dialogus, Cambridge: J. Hall, 1846 (archive.org scan, Greek text with English notes). Greek read from the pdftotext text layer and checked by eye against a 260-dpi render of each PDF page; printed page = running header. Not Otto's text; Trollope's own base text not checked.
english: in Christ the Son of God, who was proclaimed as about to come to all the world, to be the everlasting law and the everlasting covenant
edition: Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 1, Buffalo: Christian Literature Publishing Co., 1885 (New Advent revision, Kevin Knight); chapter numbers only, no page numbers | Greek: Trollope 1846 (Cambridge: J. Hall)
what_it_says: Justin calls the Christ born of the Virgin 'Son of God', proclaimed to come as the everlasting law and covenant.
limits: This is the temporal-birth worry: 'born' (gennētheis) is said of the birth from a virgin, not of an eternal generation; the sentence does not say when the Son was begotten.

ref: Dial. 48.1 (Trypho's paraphrase: pre-existent God made man)
greek: τὸ γὰρ λέγειν σε προϋπάρχειν Θεὸν ὄντα πρὸ αἰώνων τοῦτον τὸν Χριστόν, εἶτα καὶ γεννηθῆναι ἄνθρωπον γενόμενον ὑπομεῖναι, καὶ ὅτι οὐκ ἄνθρωπος ἐξ ἀνθρώπου, οὐ μόνον παράδοξον δοκεῖ μοι εἶναι, ἀλλὰ καὶ μωρόν.
greek_edition: W. Trollope (ed.), S. Justini philosophi et martyris cum Tryphone Judaeo dialogus, Cambridge: J. Hall, 1846 (archive.org scan, Greek text with English notes). Greek read from the pdftotext text layer and checked by eye against a 260-dpi render of each PDF page; printed page = running header. Not Otto's text; Trollope's own base text not checked.
english: For when you say that this Christ existed as God before the ages, then that He submitted to be born and become man, yet that He is not man of man, this [assertion] appears to me to be not merely paradoxical, but also foolish.
edition: Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 1, Buffalo: Christian Literature Publishing Co., 1885 (New Advent revision, Kevin Knight); chapter numbers only, no page numbers | Greek: Trollope 1846 (Cambridge: J. Hall)
what_it_says: Trypho states the objection that Justin's teaching is that Christ existed as God before the ages, was born man, and was not of human seed.
limits: Trypho's paraphrase; it is the best statement of the pre-existence claim that Justin is asked to defend, and it is the opponent's wording, not Justin's.

ref: Dial. 48.2 (Justin concedes he cannot prove pre-existence)
greek: οὐκ ἀπόλλυται τὸ τοῦτον εἶναι Χριστὸν τοῦ Θεοῦ, ἐὰν ἀποδεῖξαι μὴ δύνωμαι ὅτι καὶ προϋπῆρχεν υἱὸς τοῦ ποιητοῦ τῶν ὅλων, Θεὸς ὤν, καὶ γεγέννηται ἄνθρωπος διὰ τῆς παρθένου. Ἀλλὰ ἐκ παντὸς ἀποδεικνυμένου ὅτι οὗτός ἐστιν
greek_edition: W. Trollope (ed.), S. Justini philosophi et martyris cum Tryphone Judaeo dialogus, Cambridge: J. Hall, 1846 (archive.org scan, Greek text with English notes). Greek read from the pdftotext text layer and checked by eye against a 260-dpi render of each PDF page; printed page = running header. Not Otto's text; Trollope's own base text not checked.
english: though I be unable to prove that He existed formerly as Son of the Maker of all things, being God, and was born a man by the Virgin.
edition: Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 1, Buffalo: Christian Literature Publishing Co., 1885 (New Advent revision, Kevin Knight); chapter numbers only, no page numbers | Greek: Trollope 1846 (Cambridge: J. Hall)
what_it_says: Justin says that even if he cannot prove that Christ existed before as Son of the Maker, being God, and was born a man of the Virgin, the claim that Jesus is the Christ still stands.
limits: Justin explicitly leaves pre-existence unproven here; a Nicene reading needs his proof elsewhere (Dial. 61-62, 126-129, outside J4). The Greek lead-in 'Ἤν μέντοι' (breathing read from the image only) is omitted.

ref: Dial. 49.1 (Spirit of God in Elijah, then in John)
greek: οὗ καὶ πρώτης φανερώσεως κῆρυξ προῆλθε τὸ ἐν Ἠλίᾳ γενόμενον πνεῦμα τοῦ Θεοῦ, ἐν Ἰωάννῃ, τῷ γενομένῳ ἐν τῷ γένει ὑμῶν προφήτῃ
greek_edition: W. Trollope (ed.), S. Justini philosophi et martyris cum Tryphone Judaeo dialogus, Cambridge: J. Hall, 1846 (archive.org scan, Greek text with English notes). Greek read from the pdftotext text layer and checked by eye against a 260-dpi render of each PDF page; printed page = running header. Not Otto's text; Trollope's own base text not checked.
english: whose first manifestation the Spirit of God who was in Elijah preceded as herald in [the person of] John
edition: Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 1, Buffalo: Christian Literature Publishing Co., 1885 (New Advent revision, Kevin Knight); chapter numbers only, no page numbers | Greek: Trollope 1846 (Cambridge: J. Hall)
what_it_says: Justin says the Spirit of God that was in Elijah went before Christ's first coming as herald in John.
limits: The 'spirit of God' is a gift of prophecy passed from Elijah to John (Dial. 49.2-3, Joshua parallel), not a distinct person. The Greek 'πνεῦμα τοῦ Θεοῦ' is exactly the 'power' worry opponents raise.

ref: Dial. 50.1 (Trypho: show another God besides the Maker)
greek: Ἀπόκριναι οὖν μοι πρότερον, πῶς ἔχεις ἀποδεῖξαι ὅτι καὶ ἄλλος Θεὸς παρὰ τὸν ποιητὴν τῶν ὅλων, καὶ τότε ἀποδείξεις ὅτι καὶ γεννηθῆναι διὰ τῆς παρθένου ὑπέμεινε.
greek_edition: W. Trollope (ed.), S. Justini philosophi et martyris cum Tryphone Judaeo dialogus, Cambridge: J. Hall, 1846 (archive.org scan, Greek text with English notes). Greek read from the pdftotext text layer and checked by eye against a 260-dpi render of each PDF page; printed page = running header. Not Otto's text; Trollope's own base text not checked.
english: Answer me then, first, how you can show that there is another God besides the Maker of all things; and then you will show, [further], that He submitted to be born of the Virgin.
edition: Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 1, Buffalo: Christian Literature Publishing Co., 1885 (New Advent revision, Kevin Knight); chapter numbers only, no page numbers | Greek: Trollope 1846 (Cambridge: J. Hall)
what_it_says: Trypho asks Justin first to show that there is another God besides the Maker of all things, and only then that the Christ submitted to be born of the Virgin.
limits: The phrase 'another God' (allos theos) is Trypho's, not Justin's; the brief attributed it to ch. 55, but it first occurs here in Trypho's mouth. Justin's own uses of 'another God' come after ch. 55 (Dial. 56 onward, outside J4; not checked here).

ref: Dial. 54.3 (Holy Spirit always present in power)
greek: Στολὴν γὰρ αὐτοῦ ἐκάλεσε τὸ ἅγιον πνεῦμα τοὺς δι' αὐτοῦ ἄφεσιν ἁμαρτιῶν λαβόντας, ἐν οἷς ἀεὶ δυνάμει μὲν πάρεστι, καὶ ἐναργῶς δὲ παρέσται ἐν τῇ δευτέρᾳ αὐτοῦ παρουσίᾳ.
greek_edition: W. Trollope (ed.), S. Justini philosophi et martyris cum Tryphone Judaeo dialogus, Cambridge: J. Hall, 1846 (archive.org scan, Greek text with English notes). Greek read from the pdftotext text layer and checked by eye against a 260-dpi render of each PDF page; printed page = running header. Not Otto's text; Trollope's own base text not checked.
english: For the Holy Spirit called those who receive remission of sins through Him, His garments; among whom He is always present in power, but will be manifestly present at His second coming.
edition: Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 1, Buffalo: Christian Literature Publishing Co., 1885 (New Advent revision, Kevin Knight); chapter numbers only, no page numbers | Greek: Trollope 1846 (Cambridge: J. Hall)
what_it_says: Justin says the Holy Spirit is 'always present in power' among those who receive forgiveness through Christ, and will be manifestly present at the second coming.
limits: The Spirit is said to be 'present in power' (dynamei), which is the wording the brief calls the 'power of God' worry; Justin does not say here that the Spirit is a person distinct from God.

ref: Dial. 54.3 (Christ's blood from the power of God, not human seed)
greek: ἀλλ' οὐκ ἐξ ἀνθρώπου σπέρματος, ἀλλ' ἐκ τῆς τοῦ Θεοῦ δυνάμεως. Ὃν γὰρ τρόπον τὸ τῆς ἀμπέλου αἷμα οὐκ ἄνθρωπος ἐγέννησεν, ἀλλὰ Θεός, οὕτως καὶ τὸ τοῦ Χριστοῦ αἷμα οὐκ ἐξ ἀνθρωπείου γένους ἔσεσθαι, ἀλλ' ἐκ Θεοῦ δυνάμεως προεμήνυσεν.
greek_edition: W. Trollope (ed.), S. Justini philosophi et martyris cum Tryphone Judaeo dialogus, Cambridge: J. Hall, 1846 (archive.org scan, Greek text with English notes). Greek read from the pdftotext text layer and checked by eye against a 260-dpi render of each PDF page; printed page = running header. Not Otto's text; Trollope's own base text not checked.
english: Christ derives blood not from the seed of man, but from the power of God.
edition: Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 1, Buffalo: Christian Literature Publishing Co., 1885 (New Advent revision, Kevin Knight); chapter numbers only, no page numbers | Greek: Trollope 1846 (Cambridge: J. Hall)
what_it_says: Justin says Christ has his blood not from human seed but from the power of God, as the vine's blood is produced by God and not by a man.
limits: Justin uses 'power of God' for the origin of Christ's flesh, not for the Spirit; the passage is about the virginal birth, not about the Spirit's personhood or eternal generation.

ref: Dial. 55.1 (Trypho: the Spirit of prophecy admits another God)
greek: Τανῦν δὲ ἤδη ἀναλαβὼν τὸν λόγον ἀπόδειξον ἡμῖν ὅτι ἕτερος Θεὸς παρὰ τὸν ποιητὴν τῶν ὅλων ὑπὸ τοῦ προφητικοῦ πνεύματος ὁμολογεῖται εἶναι,
greek_edition: W. Trollope (ed.), S. Justini philosophi et martyris cum Tryphone Judaeo dialogus, Cambridge: J. Hall, 1846 (archive.org scan, Greek text with English notes). Greek read from the pdftotext text layer and checked by eye against a 260-dpi render of each PDF page; printed page = running header. Not Otto's text; Trollope's own base text not checked.
english: show us that the Spirit of prophecy admits another God besides the Maker of all things
edition: Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 1, Buffalo: Christian Literature Publishing Co., 1885 (New Advent revision, Kevin Knight); chapter numbers only, no page numbers | Greek: Trollope 1846 (Cambridge: J. Hall)
what_it_says: Trypho asks Justin to show that the prophetic Spirit confesses another God besides the Maker of all things, after setting aside the sun and moon and the 'God of gods' passages.
limits: Trypho's request, not Justin's claim; the Greek 'ἕτερος Θεός' is the phrase the brief quotes, and it is Trypho's, placed before Justin's answer in Dial. 55-56.

ref: Dial. 36.2 (editor's note on 'from His own person')
greek: ἀπὸ τοῦ ἰδίου. We have here a plain acknowledgement of the distinct personality of the Holy Ghost. See on Apol. i. cc. 6, 5.; 60, 22.
greek_edition: W. Trollope (ed.), 1846, English note 38 to Dial. 36, read from the scan (PDF p. 87) and checked by eye.
english: 38. ἀπὸ τοῦ ἰδίου. We have here a plain acknowledgement of the distinct personality of the Holy Ghost.
edition: Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 1, Buffalo: Christian Literature Publishing Co., 1885 (New Advent revision, Kevin Knight); chapter numbers only, no page numbers | Greek: Trollope 1846 (Cambridge: J. Hall)
what_it_says: The 19th-century editor Trollope reads the Dial. 36 phrase 'from His own person' as Justin's acknowledgement of the Spirit's distinct personhood.
limits: This is an editor's gloss (English), not Justin's text; it is secondary evidence and should be cited as Trollope's reading, not Justin's.
